resources.name: Mobbin
resources.note: Every onboarding, paywall and empty state you'll ever need to copy the structure of.

resources.name: Interface In Game
resources.note: Game UI, catalogued by genre and element. The best cure for a menu that feels like a form.

resources.name: ShotDeck
resources.note: Film stills searchable by colour, lens and lighting. Where hero art and palettes should start.

resources.name: Aesthetics Wiki
resources.note: A sprawling taxonomy of visual subcultures. Useful for naming a direction so a model can hold it.

resources.name: Deck Gallery
resources.note: Real pitch decks. Slide-level lessons in saying one thing per screen.

resources.name: Component Gallery
resources.note: One component, every design system's take on it, side by side. Settle an API argument in a minute.

resources.name: Beautiful UI
resources.note: Polished UI pieces worth reverse-engineering when generated output looks flat.

resources.name: Generative Loaders
resources.note: Loading states with a point of view. Copy one instead of shipping another spinner.

resources.name: Logosystem
resources.note: Marks collected and dissected. Good for finding a shape before you touch a generator.

resources.name: Rebrand Gallery
resources.note: Before-and-after identity work. Watching what got cut teaches more than the finished mark.

resources.name: OG Image Gallery
resources.note: Social cards done well. The one asset vibe-coded projects always forget.

resources.name: Microcopy
resources.note: Button, error and empty-state wording that sounds human. Fixes the LLM voice fast.

resources.name: Really Good Emails
resources.note: Thousands of emails with the HTML. Layout ideas that survive constraints.

resources.name: Amicro
resources.note: React library of micro-interactions and component transitions.

resources.name: OriginKit
resources.note: Animated, accessible components delivered wherever you work — editor, canvas, or an MCP server that hands agents real components instead of hallucinated ones.

resources.name: Nexvyn UI
resources.note: Pre-built, reusable UI components to drop into an app.

resources.name: Untitled UI React
resources.note: The React build of the Untitled UI kit — a large, consistent component set.

resources.name: awesome-shadcn/ui
resources.note: A curated list of everything built around shadcn/ui — blocks, tools, themes and extensions, in one place.

resources.name: 21st.dev
resources.note: Registry of shadcn-compatible React components, installable by command.

resources.name: Magic UI
resources.note: Animated components for React and Tailwind, built on Motion.

resources.name: Aceternity UI
resources.note: Motion-heavy React blocks and full page sections.

resources.name: SRCL
resources.note: Open-source React components and styles with terminal aesthetics.

resources.name: Fancy Components
resources.note: Docs-first collection of playful React components and effects.

resources.name: Dice UI
resources.note: Accessible shadcn/ui components in React, TypeScript and Tailwind.

resources.name: React Bits
resources.note: Animated React components to drop into a page.

resources.name: Tremor
resources.note: React components for dashboards and charts.

resources.name: Reverse UI
resources.note: 68+ animated UI components, ready to drop in.

resources.name: Tamagui
resources.note: Universal UI system for React Native and web, with an optimising compiler.

resources.name: Animate UI
resources.note: Animated React components.

resources.name: Motion Primitives
resources.note: Animated component primitives built with Motion.

resources.name: tweakcn
resources.note: Visual theme editor for shadcn/ui — tune the tokens, export the CSS.

resources.name: codetocanvas
resources.note: Lays out every screen of a React prototype on one zoomable board, live and joined by flow arrows. Review the whole thing at once instead of clicking through it.

resources.name: agent-annotate
resources.note: Click an element or drag over a region of your local page, and the note goes straight into your coding agent's chat. Faster than writing out a screenshot's worth of words.

resources.name: Unslop
resources.note: An agent skill that strips 33 kinds of AI tells from a draft, from hedging to em-dash habits. Run it on anything a model wrote before it ships.

resources.name: Cleaning copy
resources.note: A ladder for deciding whether a UI string should exist at all before you polish it. Most interface copy gets better by being deleted.

resources.name: better-writing
resources.note: Jakub Krehel's skill for interface copy: clear errors, consistent terms, and a tone that shifts without leaving the product's voice.

resources.name: DialKit
resources.note: Josh Puckett's live sliders, colour pickers and spring editors bound to your running UI. Tune the feel by hand instead of guessing numbers in code.

resources.name: Agentation
resources.note: Click elements, leave notes, and hand your agent exact selectors and component paths instead of 'the button on the left'.

resources.name: Gooey.AI
resources.note: Fork a working AI agent workflow and put it on WhatsApp, voice or web without building the plumbing. Handy for testing a conversational idea with real people.

resources.name: show-me
resources.note: HumanLayer's skill that makes your agent explain with a diagram or a small HTML page instead of a wall of text. It picks the smallest picture that makes the point.

resources.name: Hallmark
resources.note: Nutlope's skill against generic-looking AI design, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Install it before you ask for a landing page.

resources.name: Taste Skill
resources.note: Gives your agent opinions about layout, type and spacing so the first draft isn't the same page everyone else got.

resources.name: Open Design
resources.note: Open-source, local-first alternative to Claude Design. Your coding agent makes the prototypes, decks and dashboards.

resources.name: Leva
resources.note: pmndrs' React panel of live controls. One hook and every value you're unsure about gets a slider.

resources.name: Tufte chart skill
resources.note: Turns 'make me a chart' into something Edward Tufte would sign off on: less ink, more data.

resources.name: Syntax Style
resources.note: Sentence-level writing craft from Virginia Tufte's Artful Sentences, as a skill. For when the copy is correct but flat.

resources.name: Make Interfaces Feel Better
resources.note: Jakub Krehel's list of small details that make UI feel crafted, packaged so your agent applies them for you.

resources.name: Huashu Design
resources.note: A full design skill for Claude Code: high-fidelity prototypes, slides and animation in HTML, with a built-in design review and MP4 export.

resources.name: UI Design Brain
resources.note: Best practices and conventions for 60+ UI components, so your agent builds a date picker like someone who has used one.

resources.name: Plannotator
resources.note: Mark up your agent's plan or diff visually and send the notes back in one click. Review before it builds the wrong thing.

resources.name: Medal Forge
resources.note: Drop in an SVG and get a 3D medal, badge or metal plate, with GLB, USDZ, GIF and MOV export.

resources.name: Pi Design Deck
resources.note: Your agent shows design options as slides with live previews, and you pick one. Built for the Pi agent.

resources.name: UI Sound Design
resources.note: Describe a click or chime in plain words and get working Web Audio or Tone.js code back.

resources.name: playhtml
resources.note: Add one attribute and an HTML element becomes interactive and shared by everyone on the page. Small, playful, a bit magic.

resources.name: Agent Sprite Forge
resources.note: Sprite sheets, maps and animated GIFs from a prompt, with transparent PNG frames ready for a 2D game.

resources.name: Sprite Sheet Creator
resources.note: Make a playable 2D character and map from a prompt, powered by fal.ai.

resources.name: Node Banana
resources.note: Free, open node canvas for chaining image-generation steps. See the whole pipeline instead of a chat log.

resources.name: OFL Font Baker
resources.note: A macOS app for building one composite font out of several open-licence fonts.

resources.name: Awful AI
resources.note: A running list of harmful uses of AI. Worth reading before you design the next feature that decides something about people.

resources.name: Interaction Kit
resources.note: Armond Schneider's copy-ready React components for the quiet details: image expands, notification reveals, pickers. The polish pass, already done.

resources.name: Interface Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Better and worse versions side by side for animation, type, colour, layout, accessibility and copy. Keep it open during a UI review.

resources.name: here.now
resources.note: Your agent publishes an HTML page or file to a live URL in seconds. The fastest way to put a prototype in front of someone.

resources.name: Impeccable
resources.note: When an AI-made page looks sloppy, this skill critiques and fixes the layout, type, colour and spacing. A design pass in one command.

resources.name: Data Vizard
resources.note: Turns the data-viz process into a step-by-step wizard your agent guides you through: find the data, analyse, pick a story, design, critique.

resources.name: Emil Kowalski's skills
resources.note: Free animation skills from Emil Kowalski, like one that finds where your UI should move. Knowing a few motion terms gets you much more out of them.

resources.name: Designer Skills
resources.note: A big set of agent skills for design work from research through systems, UI, interaction and handoff.

resources.name: Creative Coding Concept Coach
resources.note: A skill that helps you sharpen a generative or data-driven art idea before any code, as a thinking partner rather than a shortcut.

resources.name: Variant
resources.note: Describe an idea and scroll through endless UI designs for it. Good for finding a direction before you build.

resources.name: DiffUI
resources.note: Generates several on-brand UI options at once, then turns the one you pick into responsive code.

resources.name: Awesome Creative Coding JS Libraries
resources.note: Rasagy's pick of JavaScript libraries for charts, generative art and creative coding. Naming the right library gets your agent a much better result.

resources.name: FIFA World Cup 2026 data stories
resources.note: Data stories from one dataset built with different prompt structures. A clear lesson in how much the prompt shapes the chart.

resources.name: From Data to Viz
resources.note: A decision tree from the shape of your data to the charts that suit it, with the common mistakes for each. Use it before you ask for 'a chart'.

resources.name: How to AI Code
resources.note: Kenneth's free, beginner-friendly guide to building and shipping your first site with AI. Redo the workshop or pass it on.

resources.name: Lucide
resources.note: The default icon set for shadcn/ui, and the one most agents reach for. Clean 24px strokes, ISC licence.

resources.name: Phosphor Icons
resources.note: Six weights of every icon, from thin to duotone. Pick a weight to match your type instead of settling. MIT.

resources.name: Heroicons
resources.note: From the Tailwind team: outline, solid and mini sizes that sit perfectly next to Tailwind UI. MIT.

resources.name: Tabler Icons
resources.note: Nearly 6,000 consistent stroke icons, so you rarely have to mix sets to find an odd one. MIT.

resources.name: Iconoir
resources.note: A calm, slightly softer stroke set for when Lucide feels too familiar. MIT.

resources.name: Radix Icons
resources.note: A small, crisp 15px set drawn for dense interfaces and toolbars. MIT.

resources.name: Remix Icon
resources.note: Every icon in both line and fill, which makes on/off and selected states easy. Free for any project, but its own licence bars reselling it as an icon pack.

resources.name: Icônes
resources.note: Anthony Fu's search across 150+ open icon sets at once. Copy an SVG or the exact import line for your agent.

resources.name: The Shape of AI
resources.note: A pattern library for AI products: how to show prompts, sources, confidence and control. Start here before designing a chat box.

resources.name: AI Design Field Guide
resources.note: Techniques from the designers behind OpenAI, Anthropic, Figma and Notion, written up as methods you can try.

resources.name: Articulate
resources.note: The words designers use when they know what they're looking at. Name what you want and the agent gets closer.

resources.name: abtest.design
resources.note: Real A/B test results from well-known apps. Evidence for a design argument instead of taste.

resources.name: Built by Designers
resources.note: Apps, tools and experiments that designers built and shipped themselves. Proof it can be done, and ideas for what to make.

resources.name: Branding Style Guides
resources.note: An archive of real brand guideline PDFs. See how a system is documented before you ask an agent to follow one.

resources.name: YOYOYO
resources.note: A made-up brand by Google DeepMind and Porto Rocha, built with Nano Banana Pro. What AI in serious brand work can look like.

resources.name: Smallbits
resources.note: 290+ pixel icons on an 8×8 grid, free for personal and commercial use. Charm for when a stroke set feels too polite.

resources.name: UX Pilot
resources.note: Generates wireframes and UI screens from a prompt. Quick for exploring layouts before you commit to one.

resources.name: Osmo
resources.note: An AI video editor for launch videos and motion graphics. Feed it Figma files or footage; it builds the animation as editable code.

resources.name: Lapis
resources.note: Kontinentalist's no-code tool for data stories that mix text, charts and visuals. From the team behind some of Asia's best data journalism.

resources.name: The Moving Poster
resources.note: A gallery of animated posters. Good for seeing how little motion a layout needs to come alive.

resources.name: GenCup
resources.note: Every 2026 World Cup match turned into a generative poster. Football data, code and graphic design in one.

resources.name: Angle Ref
resources.note: Openly licensed photos of people, searchable by head direction. Reference for illustration and AI image prompts.

resources.name: Recode Project
resources.note: Early computer art redrawn in modern code, with the source for each piece. A generative-art history you can fork.

resources.name: sitescroll
resources.note: An endless scroll of personal websites. The antidote to every portfolio template looking the same.

resources.name: Contraire
resources.note: A panel of AI readers argues with your draft, points out the weak spots and hands back a sharper version.

resources.name: Process Pamphlets
resources.note: One design project per issue from start to finish, told through emails, sketches, drafts and screenshots.

resources.name: Methods for Random Gradients
resources.note: Justin Jay Wang on the gradients he made at OpenAI: noise heightmaps, layered SVG radials and AI-generated ones, with hundreds of examples.

resources.name: AI Prototyping: Harder, Worser, Faster, Wronger
resources.note: Anna E. Cook on why a polished AI prototype can skip the thinking a prototype is for. Decide what you're testing before you open a tool.

resources.name: State of AI Design 2026
resources.note: Designer Fund and Foundation Capital's yearly report on how design teams really use AI: tools, craft and team shape. Data for the 'are we behind?' conversation.

resources.name: Katie Dill: scaling intent, quality and artistry with AI
resources.note: Stripe's head of design on avoiding 'zombie UI': keep a point of view, build your standards into the AI tools, and edit well past the first draft.

resources.name: Dan Shipper: run your product team like a research lab
resources.note: Every's CEO on keeping a small lab that tries new AI capabilities in real work while the main team improves what already ships.

resources.name: Agentic Brand Systems
resources.note: Little Plains on writing a brand's decisions and reasoning down so both people and agents can apply it. The fix for brand drift when everyone ships with AI.

resources.name: Murmur
resources.note: Shape a responsive glass orb for an AI interface. A presence that listens and thinks, instead of another spinner.

resources.name: Orbkit
resources.note: Reactive shader orbs to drop into an AI interface, so the assistant has a presence while it listens and thinks.

resources.name: Drawably
resources.note: UI controls that look drawn with a pen. A quick way to make a prototype feel like a sketch, or a product feel human.

resources.name: Painterly
resources.note: Loading animations with a painted, hand-made feel that you copy as code. Nicer than a spinner.

resources.name: ShaderGradient
resources.note: Moving 3D gradients you tune by hand and export for React, Figma or Framer. The fast route to a living hero section.

resources.name: doppio
resources.note: Motion templates for presenting design work. Makes a portfolio shot or launch post move without opening After Effects.

resources.name: Colors & Fonts
resources.note: Colour palettes, font pairings and contrast checks in one place. Pick a starting point to hand your agent.

resources.name: Design Your Sunset
resources.note: Build a sunset gradient by hand and export it. A small, lovely tool for backgrounds and brand colour.

resources.name: Textures
resources.note: Tactile image filters that run in the browser. Takes the flat, rendered edge off a picture.

resources.name: ASCIInator
resources.note: Turns images into finely tuned ASCII art. For terminal-flavoured heroes and loading states.

resources.name: Shake it to Shape it
resources.note: Generates polished SVG shapes for blobs, badges and decorative forms.

resources.name: BuilderTools
resources.note: Free browser tools for making design assets. The small jobs you'd otherwise open a big app for.

resources.name: Annual Report Archive
resources.note: 3,000+ corporate annual reports from 1945 to 1991. Peak editorial and information design, all in one place.

resources.name: Personal Sites (Are.na)
resources.note: A hand-picked Are.na channel of personal websites with real character. Look here before you ask an agent for 'a portfolio'.
